paragraphs.source_en: Then the thumping of the Fading Dirge begins. Fists on chests. Thousands. Fast, like a racing heartbeat. Slower. A beat a second. A beat every five. Every ten. Then never again, and the mournful mass fades away like dust held in the palm as the old tunnels wail with deep winds.

units.source_en: Then the thumping of the Fading Dirge begins.
Fists on chests.
Thousands.
Fast, like a racing heartbeat.
Slower.
A beat a second.
A beat every five.
Every ten.
Then never again, and the mournful mass fades away like dust held in the palm as the old tunnels wail with deep winds.

paragraphs.source_en: And the Golds, they fly away.

units.source_en: And the Golds, they fly away.

paragraphs.source_en: Eo’s father, Loran, and Kieran sit by my door through the night. They say they are there to keep me company. But they are there to guard me, to ensure I do not die. I want to die. Mother dresses my wound with silk my sister, Leanna, stole from the Webbery.

They say they are there to keep me company.

ja.t: らは、ぼくのそばにいるためだと

units.source_en: But they are there to guard me, to ensure I do not die.
I want to die.
Mother dresses my wound with silk my sister, Leanna, stole from the Webbery.

paragraphs.source_en: “Keep the nervenucleic dry, or you will scar.”

units.source_en: “Keep the nervenucleic dry, or you will scar.”

paragraphs.source_en: What are scars? How little they matter. Eo will not see them, so why should I care? She will not run her hand along my back. She will never kiss my wounds.

units.source_en: What are scars?
How little they matter.

ja.t: そんなものは、どうでもいい。

units.source_en: Eo will not see them, so why should I care?

ja.t: ることはない。なら、なぜぼくが

units.source_en: She will not run her hand along my back.

ja.t: をすべらせることはない。

units.source_en: She will never kiss my wounds.
She is gone.

paragraphs.source_en: I lie in our bed on my back so I can feel the pain and forget my wife. But I cannot forget. She hangs even now. In the morning, I will pass her on the way to the mines. Soon she will stink and soon she will rot. My beautiful wife shone too bright to live long. I still feel her neck cracking against my hands; they tremble now in the night.

But I cannot forget.
She hangs even now.
In the morning, I will pass her on the way to the mines.
Soon she will stink and soon she will rot.

ja.t: きるにはあまりにもまぶしく

units.source_en: I still feel her neck cracking against my hands; they tremble now in the night.

paragraphs.source_en: There is a hidden tunnel I carved in my bedroom long ago in the rock so I could sneak out as a child. I use it now. I leave out the secret path, climbing stealthily down from my home, so my kin never see me slip away in the low light.

units.source_en: There is a hidden tunnel I carved in my bedroom long ago in the rock so I could sneak out as a child.
I use it now.
I leave out the secret path, climbing stealthily down from my home, so my kin never see me slip away in the low light.

paragraphs.source_en: It is quiet in the township. Quiet except for the HC, which makes my wife die to a soundtrack. They intended to show the futility of disobedience. And they succeed in that, but there is something else in the video. They show my flogging, and Eo’s, and they play her song throughout. And as she dies, they play it again, which seems to give the video the wrong effect. Even if she were not my wife, I see a martyr, a young girl’s pretty song silenced by the rope of cruel men.

And as she dies, they play it again, which seems to give the video the wrong effect.
Even if she were not my wife, I see a martyr, a young girl’s pretty song silenced by the rope of cruel men.

ja.t: でなかったとしても、ぼくには

paragraphs.source_en: Then the HC flashes black for several moments. It has never gone to black before. And Octavia au Lune comes back on with the same old message. It almost seems as though someone has hacked into the broadcast, because my wife flickers onto the giant screen again.

paragraphs.source_en: “Break the chains!” she cries. Then she’s gone and the screen is black. It crackles. The image comes back. She cries it again. Black once more. Standard programming goes up, then it cuts to her screaming one last time and then there’s me pulling her legs. Then static.

she cries.

Black once more.
Standard programming goes up, then it cuts to her screaming one last time and then there’s me pulling her legs.
Then static.
